response.sql: WITH total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM Order_Items), per_product AS (SELECT p.product_id, p.production_type_code, AVG(CAST(oi.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_qty, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS item_cnt, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) * 1.0 / (SELECT n FROM total) AS item_share FROM Products p LEFT JOIN Order_Items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.production_type_code), per_type AS (SELECT pc.product_type_description, AVG(pp.avg_qty) AS avg_qty, AVG(pp.item_cnt) AS avg_cnt, AVG(pp.item_share) AS avg_share FROM per_product pp JOIN Product_Categories pc ON pc.production_type_code = pp.production_type_code GROUP BY pc.product_type_description) SELECT AVG(avg_qty) AS avg_of_avg_quantity, AVG(avg_cnt) AS avg_of_order_item_count, AVG(avg_share) AS avg_of_order_item_share FROM per_type;

assumptions.assumption: product_quantity is stored as text and is cast to a number for averaging; non-numeric or NULL values are ignored by AVG.
Share of all order items = the product's order item count divided by the total row count of Order_Items.
All products are included, even those never ordered. They have an order item count of 0 and share of 0, and a NULL average quantity that is ignored.
Product types are grouped by product_type_description, so categories with the same description are merged. The average over types is the unweighted mean of per-type averages.

alternatives.interpretation: Only products that appear in at least one order item are included. Never-ordered products are excluded rather than counted as 0.
